papers.title: Engineering Methylobacterium as a C1 biomanufacturing platform: Metabolic architecture, regulatory networks, and synthetic biology strategies.
papers.abstract: Methanol is emerging as a sustainable and energy-dense one carbon (C1) feedstock for next-generation biomanufacturing, owing to its superior energy density, abundance, water miscibility, and decoupling from food supply chains. Methylobacterium species are facultative methylotrophs that have evolved sophisticated metabolic and regulatory networks for efficient methanol utilization. This review highlights the transition of Methylobacterium from a model organism for dissecting methylotrophy to a programmable C1 chassis for synthetic biology. We provide a unique overview of its core metabolic architecture, focusing on the lanthanide-switchable pyrroloquinoline quinone (PQQ)-dependent methanol oxidation, the tetrahydromethanopterin (H₄MPT)-mediated formaldehyde buffering system, and the tight coupling of the serine cycle with the ethylmalonyl-CoA (EMC) pathway, which together govern carbon flux, redox balance, and energy efficiency. Building on this intrinsic framework, we survey how these traits are leveraged to produce high-value chemicals, such as folate derivatives, redox cofactors, organic acids, terpenoids, bioplastics, and single-cell protein. Furthermore, we discuss advanced engineering strategies for systematic chassis optimization including global transcriptional regulation, metabolic valve control, and photo-methylotrophic configurations, along with a comprehensive evaluation of Methylobacterium chassis advantages and disadvantages, concrete product-chassis matching rules, common engineering bottlenecks, and diversified low-cost feedstock options. Finally, we propose a product-chassis matching framework and outline future directions centered on regulatory control, flux coordination, and robustness enhancement to overcome current limitations in titer, yield, and scale-up, while also leveraging agricultural applications and low-cost feedstocks, thereby positioning Methylobacterium as a cornerstone of sustainable low-carbon biotechnology.
papers.authors: Yao L, Ma Z, Liu Z, Tan L, Yang S.

papers.title: Natural and engineered bacteriophages against multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens: current landscape and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: The worldwide emergence of antimicrobial resistance and the need for non-conventional alternatives to conventional antibiotics have been increased by multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens, which cause the majority of nosocomial infections and are starting to develop resistance to even the most potent drugs. Engineered bacteriophages are promising precision antimicrobials because of their ability to selectively infect and lyse bacterial hosts, multiply at infection sites, and co-evolve with bacterial populations to overcome resistance. Advances in synthetic biology, such as tail fiber modification, depolymerase and endolysin enhancement, genome editing using the clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR), and computationally designed phage cocktails, have opened new possibilities for therapeutics that were hindered by the limitations of natural phages. These engineering strategies expand host range, enhance biofilm penetration, and target resistance genes. In spite of promising evidence in preclinical models, the use of engineered phages in routine clinical practice remains difficult. Specific key challenges include unclear regulations, lack of good manufacturing practice (GMP)grade production, variable pharmacokinetics and limited clinical trial data. This review critically examines engineering approaches to improve phage activity against ESKAPE pathogens, identifies the scientific and regulatory barriers limiting clinical use, and outlines the key steps needed for wider adoption.
papers.authors: Nautiyal D, Sahu M, Jain U.

papers.title: Engineered probiotics target granulomas to treat mycobacterial infection
papers.abstract: Granulomas are a pathological niche for mycobacteria that remain difficult to access with conventional therapies. Here we show that probiotic Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) infiltrates and colonizes granulomas and can be engineered as a delivery system that senses the local microenvironment and releases antimycobacterial payloads. Specifically, we leveraged the hypoxic microenvironment of necrotic granulomas to restrict bacterial growth, and developed a dual-mode lysis circuit combining intracellular and extracellular killing for sustained payload release with limited evolutionary escape. We further engineered EcN to express a mycobacteriophage-derived enzyme, generating a strain that suppressed drug-sensitive and drug-resistant mycobacteria in vitro and potentiated conventional antibiotic activity. Engineered probiotics also reduced mycobacterial burden in vivo, and in a murine model of rifampicin-resistant infection, combination treatment with pretomanid achieved greater bacterial reduction than either monotherapy. Together, these results establish a synthetic biology framework for targeting granulomatous infections with programmable living microbes.
papers.authors: Chen Y, Harimoto T, Makafe GG, Coker C, Kim H, Im J, Jing Y, Jin H, Hu X, Zutshi S, Raneri MR, Weinrick B, Danino T.

enrichment.titleZh: 工程化益生菌靶向肉芽肿，用于治疗分枝杆菌感染
enrichment.abstractZh: 肉芽肿是分枝杆菌的一种病理性生存微环境，常规疗法仍难以到达。本研究表明，益生菌大肠杆菌Nissle 1917（Escherichia coli Nissle 1917，EcN）能够浸润并定植于肉芽肿，还可被改造成感知局部微环境并释放抗分枝杆菌载荷的递送系统。具体而言，研究者利用坏死性肉芽肿的低氧微环境限制细菌生长，并开发了结合细胞内与细胞外杀伤的双模式裂解回路，以实现载荷持续释放，同时限制进化逃逸。研究者进一步改造EcN，使其表达一种来源于分枝杆菌噬菌体的酶，获得的菌株在体外抑制了药物敏感型和耐药型分枝杆菌，并增强了常规抗生素的活性。工程化益生菌还降低了体内分枝杆菌负荷；在利福平耐药感染的小鼠模型中，与pretomanid联合治疗实现的菌量下降幅度大于任一单药治疗。这些结果共同建立了一个利用可编程活微生物靶向肉芽肿性感染的合成生物学框架。

papers.title: Molecular Biology and Synthetic Biology-Guided Development of Recognition and Reporting Elements of Biosensor.
papers.abstract: Microbial cell biosensors are capable of detecting fluctuations in the concentrations of substances both inside and outside the cell, as well as changes in the external environment, and can generate measurable signal outputs. Microbial cell biosensors are characterized by low cost, simple operation, and high specificity. The rapid advancement of synthetic biology has significantly propelled the development and practical application of microbial cell biosensors. In this chapter, we provide a comprehensive summary of the composition and working principles of microbial cell biosensors. Additionally, we introduce various strategies and the latest progress in modifying biorecognition element and reporting elements using molecular biology and synthetic biology techniques in recent years. This book chapter offers new insights and valuable references for the research and development of microbial cell biosensors.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Meng C, Wang L, Liang B.

enrichment.titleZh: 分子生物学与合成生物学指导的生物传感器识别元件和报告元件开发
enrichment.abstractZh: 微生物细胞生物传感器能够检测细胞内外物质浓度的波动以及外部环境变化，并产生可测量的信号输出。这类传感器具有成本低、操作简单和特异性高等特点。合成生物学的快速发展显著推动了微生物细胞生物传感器的开发和实际应用。本章全面总结微生物细胞生物传感器的组成及工作原理，并介绍近年来利用分子生物学和合成生物学技术改造生物识别元件与报告元件的多种策略及最新进展，为微生物细胞生物传感器的研究与开发提供新的认识和参考。

papers.title: Beyond Cell Factory: In Vitro Biotransformation (ivBT): A Paradigm-Shifting Biomanufacturing Platform.
papers.abstract: The paradigm of industrial biomanufacturing is shifting rapidly. Microbial fermentation mediated by cell factories is the dominant platform of biomanufacturing and has a history of thousands of years. However, their inherent properties, such as self-proliferation, cellular complexity, maintenance, and bioenergetic limits, could prevent them from being the best winner of biomanufacturing, especially for biocommodities and bioenergy. In this book chapter, we introduce a new concept of in vitro biotransformation (ivBT) as an emerging biomanufacturing platform that can surpass microbial cell factory. The development of ivBT is driven by the urgent great needs of food security and a new carbon-neutral energy society in the future. In theory, ivBT can have the theoretical yield and very high volumetric productivity and could have low-cost biomanufacturing costs. Furthermore, we highlight several representative applications, such as artificial photosynthesis for CO2-to-starch synthesis, in vitro respiration that can produce hydrogen under anaerobic conditions and electricity under aerobic conditions, directed glycosidic bond rearrangement (i.e., ATP-free or low-ATP biotransformation of cellulose to starch), and healthy sugars. Industrial biomanufacturing of myo-inositol, D-tagatose, and cellulosic starch would wipe off any prejudice (e.g., costly enzymes and short lifetime) and demonstrate transformative potential of ivBT. ivBT would be a paradigm-shifting biomanufacturing platform because it is like a dimensional reduction attack that can simplify extremely complicated cell factories by decreasing their dimensions.
papers.authors: Song Z, Job Zhang YP.

papers.title: Metabolic Remodelingof the NOG Pathway and Glyoxylate Cycle for High-Yield L-Homoserine Biosynthesis.
papers.abstract: L‑homoserine is a valuable C4 amino acid with broad applications in agriculture, pharmaceuticals, and daily chemicals. However, existing high‑yielding strains have mainly been evaluated at laboratory scale, and their scale‑up feasibility has not yet been sufficiently verified, leaving industrial production without a direct engineering basis. In this study, a non-auxotrophic, scalable L‑homoserine high‑producer was constructed by targeting carbon loss, rewiring the metabolic network, and maintaining cofactor balance. Specifically, the threonine branch was dynamically attenuated to reduce product degradation, while the non‑oxidative glycolysis (NOG) pathway was introduced and coupled with the glyoxylate shunt to conserve carbon and redirect flux toward the aspartate pathway, thereby increasing precursor availability. The main biosynthetic pathway and cofactor regeneration were further strengthened to accelerate L‑homoserine synthesis. Ultimately, strain HS25 achieved a titer of 126.5 g/L L‑homoserine,a yield of 0.58 g/g glucose, and a productivity of 1.77 g/L/hin 50 L fermentation. These metabolic engineering strategies are scalable and may serve as a generalizable framework for the industrial production of other aspartate‑derived amino acids and their derivatives.
papers.authors: Shan Q, Zhang J, Gong R, Zhou Y, Xu J, Liu Z, Zheng Y.

papers.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
papers.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.
papers.authors: Xiang M, Su B, Jiang C, Sun T.

enrichment.titleZh: 人工细胞与仿生细胞：推动药物发现和递送范式转变的智能系统
enrichment.abstractZh: 合成生物学、材料科学与人工智能的融合正推动生物制药研究发生变革，使其从被动药物载体发展为智能、可编程的治疗系统。本综述将人工细胞与仿生细胞作为连接基础生物学发现和临床转化的框架进行评估，并考察了5条关键技术路径：膜工程化人工细胞、无膜细胞器（MLO）系统、多区室人工细胞、原始细胞通讯网络及虚拟细胞。这些平台能够精确调控药物稳定性、靶向性、生物合成及适应性响应能力。近期进展包括微环境触发释放、逻辑门控的细胞间通讯，以及虚拟细胞辅助的高通量筛选和毒性预测。尽管取得这些进展，可规模化制造、长期稳定性及监管适配仍面临挑战。将闭环学习、可解释模型与先进生物制造相整合，将是推动人工细胞与仿生细胞系统走向下一代精准医学前沿的关键。

papers.title: Yeast Surface Display of Artificial Multienzyme Complexes for Enhanced Production of Rebaudioside M.
papers.abstract: Rebaudioside M (Reb M) is an ideal low-calorie natural sweetener with excellent sensory properties and well-established safety profile. Industrial production of Reb M is limited by low natural abundance and the bottlenecks of existing biomanufacturing strategies, including low productivity, intermediate accumulation and high enzyme costs. Here, a novel biosynthetic platform based on yeast surface display of artificial multienzyme complexes was established for efficient Reb M production. The artificial protein scaffold containing multiple orthogonal cohesin modules was displayed on the surface of Pichia pastoris via the AGA1 anchoring motif. Through orthogonal cohesin-dockerin interactions, Reb M biosynthetic pathway enzymes (PgUGTMut, AtSUS1 and UGT76G1Mut) with the corresponding dockerin modules were assembled on the artificial protein scaffold to form multienzyme complexes. The catalytic activity of crude glycosyltransferases was improved by isozyme screening and expression optimization with molecular chaperones. This surface-displayed system demonstrated multiple advantages. First, the multienzyme complex assembled on the yeast surface showed higher catalytic efficiency than free enzymes. Additionally, fructose was consumed by P. pastoris to drive the reaction toward Reb M biosynthesis. Furthermore, the whole-cell catalyst showed promising reusability. Ultimately, this platform enabled the production of 36.88 g/L Reb M with a yield of 91.9% from rebaudioside A (Reb A) in a 10 mL reaction system. This work provided a feasible strategy to address the key bottlenecks in Reb M biomanufacturing and offered a reference for producing other high-value natural products via multi-enzyme cascade catalysis.
papers.authors: Bao J, Qiao C, Li M, Gao J, Gao D, Ye C, Jiang X, Lian J.

papers.title: Microbial bioherbicides: Integrating bioprocessing, mechanisms of action and protein engineering for sustainable weed management.
papers.abstract: The widespread use of synthetic herbicides in agriculture has intensified concerns regarding environmental sustainability and human health, while the evolution of herbicide resistance has outpaced the discovery of new modes of action. Bioherbicides have consequently emerged as a viable alternative, comprising biologically derived compounds capable of suppressing weed growth. This review adopts an integrated perspective on microbially derived bioherbicides, following the active biomolecules from the producing strain and its fermentation conditions to their physiological targets in the plant and to the molecular strategies available for their optimization. Unlike previous reviews, which address these dimensions separately and focus mainly on secondary metabolites, particular emphasis is placed here on enzymes with herbicidal activity and on protein engineering approaches. Based on a structured literature search, 39 original studies were analyzed. Phytopathogenic fungi, mainly Fusarium, Diaporthe, Phoma, Alternaria and Trichoderma, predominate as producing organisms, followed by bacteria of the genera Streptomyces, Pseudomonas and Bacillus, and submerged fermentation using low-cost agro-industrial substrates is the prevailing production strategy. Enzymatic classes such as cutinases, lipases, cellulases, pectinases and proteases act primarily by degrading the cuticle and the cell wall, whereas secondary metabolites frequently target the photosynthetic apparatus, particularly photosystem II; most of these compounds, however, still lack a defined mode of action within established herbicide classification systems. Molecular approaches, including heterologous expression, molecular docking and metabolic engineering, remain comparatively underexplored despite their potential to enhance activity, stability and specificity. Advances in formulation stability, bioprocess scalability, mechanistic characterization and regulatory harmonization are identified as the key requirements to translate these biomolecules into commercially viable products for sustainable weed management.
papers.authors: Krein DDC, Conterato AAM, Plucinski R, Dotto GL, Dettmer A.

papers.title: Advanced cannabidiol delivery platforms: smart biomaterials, controlled release systems, and 3D-bioprinted therapeutic technologies.
papers.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-psychoactive phytocannabinoid derived from Cannabis sativa L. has gained significant attention in biomedical research due to its broad spectrum of therapeutic properties, including anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, neuroprotective, and anticancer activities. However, its clinical translation remains limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, rapid metabolism, and instability under physiological conditions. To overcome these challenges, advanced drug delivery platforms based on 3D bioprinting technologies have emerged as promising strategies for controlled and site-specific delivery of CBD. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art CBD delivery systems, including polymeric biomaterials such as PLGA, PEG derivatives, chitosan, alginate, and cellulose-based hybrids, which enhance drug stability and enable sustained release profiles. Nano- and microstructured systems, including liposomes, nanoparticles, nanoemulsions, microspheres, and electrospun nanofibers, are discussed for their ability to improve bioavailability and facilitate targeted delivery at the cellular level. Hydrogel-based platforms, particularly injectable and stimuli-responsive systems, are highlighted for their role in localised therapy and tissue engineering applications. Furthermore, the integration of 3D bioprinting technologies enables the fabrication of patient-specific scaffolds and implantable constructs for precision medicine and regenerative therapies. Stimuli-responsive systems, including pH-, temperature-, enzyme-, and externally triggered release platforms, further enhance on-demand drug release in diseased microenvironments. The biomedical applications of CBD-based systems are critically evaluated in antimicrobial therapy, wound healing, tumour-targeted cancer therapy, immunomodulation, microbiome regulation, and regenerative medicine. Finally, this review addresses current translational challenges such as drug loading efficiency, stability issues, scalability, and regulatory barriers, while highlighting future perspectives involving artificial intelligence-guided design, personalised nanomedicine, and advanced biomanufacturing technologies. Overall, CBD-based smart biomaterial platforms represent a highly promising approach for next-generation therapeutic systems with improved efficacy, safety, and clinical potential.
papers.authors: Shabbir A, Parvinzadeh Gashti M.

papers.title: Organoids and organs-on-a-chip as new approach methodologies at the convergence of cell biology and bioengineering.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of new approach methodologies (NAMs), including organoids and organs-on-a-chip (OOCs), has revealed a need for interdisciplinary dialogue between cell biologists and bioengineers to develop human models that can best complement therapeutic development. Stem cell-derived and bioengineered human tissue models are redefining how we understand human physiology and pathophysiology, offering control that traditional preclinical models cannot provide. By recapitulating complex tissue microenvironments, multi-organ interactions, and patient-specific biology, these systems are bridging long-standing gaps in the drug development and clinical application pipelines. Here, we synthesize advances in organoids, OOCs, and other bioengineered technologies for translational medicine to identify remaining gaps, including challenges in reproducibility, validation, and regulatory acceptance. Emerging opportunities at the intersection of synthetic biology, multi-omics, machine learning, and genetic engineering are positioning NAMs not merely as improved experimental tools but as foundational platforms for accelerating therapeutic discovery and enabling personalized medicine at scale.
papers.authors: Tavakol DN, Mendonca D, Baldassarri I, Maletic-Savatic M, Vunjak-Novakovic G.

papers.title: Protein resource allocation across subcellular compartments revealed by large-scale absolute quantitative proteomics in yeast.
papers.abstract: Subcellular compartmentalization within complex membrane-bound organelles is a hallmark of eukaryal life, enabling metabolic specialization through spatial segregation. Here, we compiled a dataset encompassing 300 absolute quantitative proteomes, the largest to date, across two yeast species under diverse experimental conditions. Leveraging big data analysis, formula fitting, and machine learning, quantitative correlations among protein abundance, resource allocation, and cellular phenotypes were elucidated at a system level. We found that subcellular resource distribution is highly uneven and covaries with specific growth rate. Specifically, at high specific growth rates, the protein mass fraction (PMF) from certain compartments, (e.g., nucleus) is consistently reduced, coinciding with the increasing protein resource demand from ribosomes. Meanwhile, nutrient limitation may induce resource recycling by upregulating protein resources within specific compartments (e.g., vacuole) to sustain stress adaptation. Importantly, our integrative analysis indicates that PMF from a few subcellular compartments (e.g., nucleus and ribosomes) can accurately predict yeast physiological parameters (e.g., specific growth rate, oxygen uptake rate), and a limited protein set (≥ 23) could be used to capture the variation in resource allocation across seven major subcellular compartments. Furthermore, our comparative analysis between Crabtree-positive and Crabtree-negative species across conditions illustrates that subcellular resource allocation could be shaped by multiple factors and the two species differ markedly in their robustness to environmental perturbations. In summary, the high-quality quantitative proteomic dataset for yeast species offers an unprecedented opportunity for understanding the general principles underlying subcellular resource allocation, laying foundations for precision engineering of cell factories in synthetic biology.
papers.authors: Lu H, Zhang Z, He S, Zhang Y, Wang Y, Tao F, Nielsen J.

enrichment.titleZh: 酵母大规模绝对定量蛋白质组学揭示亚细胞区室间的蛋白质资源分配
enrichment.abstractZh: 由复杂膜结合细胞器形成的亚细胞区室化是真核生命的重要特征，可通过空间分隔实现代谢功能特化。本研究汇编了涵盖300个绝对定量蛋白质组的数据集，是迄今规模最大的此类数据集，覆盖两种酵母及多种实验条件。通过大数据分析、公式拟合和机器学习，研究者在系统层面解析了蛋白质丰度、资源分配与细胞表型之间的定量关联。结果发现，亚细胞资源分布高度不均，并随比生长速率共同变化。具体而言，在较高比生长速率下，某些区室（如细胞核）的蛋白质质量分数（PMF）持续降低，同时核糖体对蛋白质资源的需求增加。另一方面，营养限制可能通过上调特定区室（如液泡）中的蛋白质资源来促进资源回收，从而维持胁迫适应。综合分析表明，少数亚细胞区室（如细胞核和核糖体）的PMF可准确预测酵母生理参数，例如比生长速率和摄氧速率；有限的蛋白质集合（≥23种）即可用于捕捉7个主要亚细胞区室间资源分配的变化。此外，对Crabtree效应阳性和阴性物种在不同条件下的比较显示，亚细胞资源分配可能受多种因素影响，两种酵母对环境扰动的稳健性存在明显差异。总体而言，这一高质量酵母定量蛋白质组数据集为理解亚细胞资源分配的一般原理提供了前所未有的机会，并为合成生物学中细胞工厂的精准工程改造奠定基础。
enrichment.sourceTitle: Protein resource allocation across subcellular compartments revealed by large-scale absolute quantitative proteomics in yeast.
enrichment.sourceAbstract: Subcellular compartmentalization within complex membrane-bound organelles is a hallmark of eukaryal life, enabling metabolic specialization through spatial segregation. Here, we compiled a dataset encompassing 300 absolute quantitative proteomes, the largest to date, across two yeast species under diverse experimental conditions. Leveraging big data analysis, formula fitting, and machine learning, quantitative correlations among protein abundance, resource allocation, and cellular phenotypes were elucidated at a system level. We found that subcellular resource distribution is highly uneven and covaries with specific growth rate. Specifically, at high specific growth rates, the protein mass fraction (PMF) from certain compartments, (e.g., nucleus) is consistently reduced, coinciding with the increasing protein resource demand from ribosomes. Meanwhile, nutrient limitation may induce resource recycling by upregulating protein resources within specific compartments (e.g., vacuole) to sustain stress adaptation. Importantly, our integrative analysis indicates that PMF from a few subcellular compartments (e.g., nucleus and ribosomes) can accurately predict yeast physiological parameters (e.g., specific growth rate, oxygen uptake rate), and a limited protein set (≥ 23) could be used to capture the variation in resource allocation across seven major subcellular compartments. Furthermore, our comparative analysis between Crabtree-positive and Crabtree-negative species across conditions illustrates that subcellular resource allocation could be shaped by multiple factors and the two species differ markedly in their robustness to environmental perturbations. In summary, the high-quality quantitative proteomic dataset for yeast species offers an unprecedented opportunity for understanding the general principles underlying subcellular resource allocation, laying foundations for precision engineering of cell factories in synthetic biology.

papers.title: Artificial Cells and Biomimetic Cells: Intelligent Systems Driving a Paradigm Shift in Drug Discovery and Delivery.
papers.abstract: The convergence of synthetic biology, materials science, and artificial intelligence drives a transformative shift in biopharmaceutical research, advancing from passive drug carriers to intelligent, programmable therapeutics. This review evaluates artificial and biomimetic cells as a framework that connects fundamental biological discovery with clinical translation. It examines five key technological pathways: membrane-engineered artificial cells, membraneless organelle (MLO) systems, multicompartmental artificial cells, protocell communication networks, and virtual cells. These platforms enable precise regulation of drug stability, targeting, biosynthesis, and adaptive responsiveness. Recent progress includes microenvironment-triggered release, logic-gated intercellular communication, and virtual cell-assisted high-throughput screening and toxicity prediction. Despite these advances, challenges remain in scalable manufacturing, long-term stability, and regulatory adaptation. The integration of closed-loop learning, interpretable models, and advanced biomanufacturing will be essential to position artificial and biomimetic cell systems at the forefront of next-generation precision medicine.
papers.authors: Xiang M, Su B, Jiang C, Sun T.

papers.title: Metabolic engineering of Escherichia coli to enhance L-serine biosynthesis
papers.abstract: Abstract L-serine, an important non-essential amino acid, is widely used in the food, pharmaceutical, feed, and cosmetic industries. However, previous studies on fermentative L-serine production by Escherichia coli have mainly focused on improving titer, whereas insufficient attention has been paid to the conversion yield, limiting its industrial economic feasibility. In this study, systematic metabolic engineering was performed to improve L-serine yield. Using H5 as the parental strain, the L-serine re-uptake-related genes sstT and tdcC were deleted based on the CRISPR/Cas9 system to generate strain H8, in which the L-serine titer increased to 5.58 g/L and the conversion yield reached 0.37 g/g. Subsequently, the L-serine biosynthetic module, L-serine transport module, and cofactor supply module were individually enhanced in H8, resulting in recombinant strains H8- abc , H8- be , and H8- pntab , respectively. The resulting strains H8- abc , H8- be , and H8- pntab produced 6.40, 5.89, and 5.59 g/L L-serine, with yields of 0.43, 0.39, and 0.37 g/g, respectively. Further combination of effective strategies in the H8 chassis generated strain H8- abc-be ; however, its L-serine production decreased. Finally, H8- abc was selected for fermentation medium optimization. After optimization, the L-serine titer reached 7.20 g/L in shake-flask fermentation, with a yield of 0.48 g/g, representing a 71.84% increase compared with the starting strain H5. These results provide a useful reference for the development of efficient E. coli strains for industrial L-serine production.

papers.title: Development of a CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing system for the extremely thermophilic bacterium Anaerocellum bescii
papers.abstract: Anaerocellum (f. Caldicellulosiruptor) bescii is an extremely thermophilic (Topt 75-78 °C) anaerobic bacterium and is also a highly efficient degrader of lignocellulose, making it a promising platform for metabolic engineering. To date, chromosomal genetic manipulations in A. bescii have required multistep procedures involving homologous recombination with integrating vectors and counterselection. Here, we demonstrate the first implementation of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in A. bescii facilitated by a thermostable Cas9 enzyme from Geobacillus stearothermophilus (GeoCas9). Delivery of heterologous CRISPR machinery via a replicating vector enabled us to individually and sequentially delete genes for lactate dehydrogenase (ldh) and pyrE in A. bescii. We then deployed this system to delete a novel target, tryptophan synthase (trpBA), generating a tryptophan auxotrophic strain of A. bescii. Using this strain, we show trpBA complementation enables selection and maintenance of a replicating vector expressing a heterologous enzymatic reporter gene.
papers.authors: Galindo JL, Conway JM.

papers.title: Metabolism-Informed Bioreactor Model for Transferring Knowledge from Fed-batch to Continuous Biomanufacturing
papers.abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells remain the dominant platform for monoclonal antibody (mAb) manufacturing, and rising demand is pushing the industry from fed-batch toward continuous operation. Continuous cultures promise sustained high cell densities and volumetric productivities, but their operation depends on reliable real-time monitoring, prediction and control. Limited intracellular observability and sparse extracellular measurements hinder this, leaving a persistent gap between mechanistic understanding and predictive deployment. Here we describe a metabolism-informed model for mAb production that embeds reactor- and intracellular-level mass balances directly within a learning architecture, while deliberately avoiding predefined kinetic rate laws and explicit steady-state assumptions. Because conservation relationships remain invariant across operating modes, this formulation provides a principled structural prior for cross-regime generalisation, positioning the model as a soft sensor for continuous bioprocesses: inferring unmeasured intracellular fluxes and one-step ahead forecasting extracellular concentrations to support process monitoring and control. Benchmarking two metabolic network sizes and three metabolic optimisation strategies, concentration predictions are indistinguishable across network sizes. Exchange flux fidelity is agnostic to solver choice, with network size mattering only for intracellular interpretability. Transferring the developed model from fed-batch to continuous operation with fine-tuning outperforming other transfer learning variants. This is consistent with the metabolic structure being invariant to mode of operation. Predicted fluxes reveal growth rate in fed-batch, rather than operating mode, as the dominant axis of metabolic variation, and identify potential regime-shift signals to guide experimental design for continuous culture characterisation. These results chart a route towards digital models sufficiently grounded in first-principles knowledge, yet adaptive for deployment under regime shifts.

papers.title: Biomanufacturing of L-Lactic Acid from Inulin Exploiting Kluyveromyces marxianus and Engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae Cell Factories.
papers.abstract: The transition to sustainable lactic acid (LA) biomanufacturing necessitates a shift from first-generation feedstocks toward residual biomass and low-pH fermentation, eliminating the costly, waste-intensive salt purification and acidification steps. This study presents a novel, two-yeast strategy designed to valorize inulin, a fructose polymer also found in cardoon roots, for high-efficiency LA production at a pH below its pKa. The key novelty of this work lies in identifying and pairing the unique physiological strengths of each organism: Kluyveromyces marxianus as the optimal yeast for inulin hydrolysis, and Saccharomyces cerevisiae as the superior host for robust LA production at low pH and high titers. We discovered that if ammonium sulphate is substituted with urea as a nitrogen source for K. marxianus cultivation, the inulinase activity increased by nearly 20-fold, significantly enhancing the initial breakdown of the substrate. Inulinase-enriched K. marxianus supernatant was then used to cultivate S. cerevisiae m850, an engineered homolactic strain, and convert inulin into L-LA. Comparing separate hydrolysis and fermentation (SHF) with simultaneous saccharification and fermentation (SSF), we achieved a maximal yield > 0.77 g/g with a final pH of 2.5. While SSF was limited by pH-induced inulinase inactivation, the SHF process achieved complete substrate conversion. These results demonstrate a promising platform for producing LA from a residual feedstock, drastically reducing impacts and downstream processing costs.
papers.authors: Milanesi R, Lorenzo RDD, Porro D, Branduardi P, Serra I.

enrichment.titleZh: 利用马克斯克鲁维酵母与工程酿酒酵母细胞工厂从菊粉生物制造L-乳酸
enrichment.abstractZh: 向可持续乳酸（LA）生物制造转型，需要从第一代原料转向剩余生物质及低pH发酵，以省去成本高、废物产生量大的盐纯化和酸化步骤。本研究提出一种新的双酵母策略，利用菊粉这种也存在于刺蓟（cardoon）根部的果糖聚合物，在低于乳酸pKa的pH条件下高效生产乳酸。工作的主要创新在于识别并配合利用两种微生物各自独特的生理优势：马克斯克鲁维酵母（Kluyveromyces marxianus）是菊粉水解的最佳酵母，酿酒酵母（Saccharomyces cerevisiae）则是更适合在低pH下稳健、高滴度生产乳酸的宿主。研究发现，培养K. marxianus时，如果以尿素替代硫酸铵作为氮源，菊粉酶活性可提高近20倍，从而显著增强底物的初始分解。随后，利用富含菊粉酶的K. marxianus培养上清培养同型乳酸发酵工程菌株S. cerevisiae m850，将菊粉转化为L-乳酸。在比较分步水解与发酵（SHF）和同步糖化与发酵（SSF）后，研究者获得了>0.77 g/g的最高得率，最终pH为2.5。SSF受到pH引起的菊粉酶失活限制，而SHF工艺实现了底物完全转化。这些结果展示了利用剩余原料生产乳酸的有前景平台，可显著降低相关影响及下游加工成本。

papers.title: Kinetic metabolic modeling of Saccharomyces cerevisiae mutants reveals two major regulatory patterns of glycolytic flux control.
papers.abstract: Maintaining a high glycolytic flux is critical for robust ethanol fermentation and metabolic engineering in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. However, the regulatory mechanisms that prevent the excess turbo design structure of glycolysis under genetic perturbations are unknown. In this study, we constructed a kinetic model of yeast central carbon metabolism encompassing 90 reactions and 543 parameters. Using a genetic algorithm, we trained the model ensemble using multi-omics datasets (proteomics, metabolomics, and fluxomics) collected from the wild-type strain and 11 single-gene deletion mutants. Metabolic control analysis (MCA) of the calibrated models revealed that two major regulatory modes governed the glycolytic flux in most of the strains examined under the culture condition used in this study, although gcr2Δ exhibited a distinct control profile and gnd1Δ could not be reproduced by the model. The wild-type, gcn4Δ, and rpe1Δ strains exhibited an HXK-limited control mode, in which lowered hexokinase activity likely acts as a feedback limiter to prevent pathway over-activation. Conversely, seven other mutants shifted to an ATP demand-coupled mode, transferring flux control to energy-dissipating reactions and linking glycolytic flux directly to ATP demand. No single motif was uniformly shared within either group, implying that strain-specific expression adjustments repeatedly resulted in two regulatory modes. These findings elucidate the robust, multimodal control strategies employed by yeast to safeguard its high fermentation capacity and provide a theoretical foundation for targeted metabolic engineering and robust bioprocess design.
papers.authors: Sato G, Yamasaki K, Okahashi N, Matsuda F.

enrichment.titleZh: 酿酒酵母突变株的动力学代谢建模揭示糖酵解通量控制的两种主要调控模式
enrichment.abstractZh: 维持高糖酵解通量，对酿酒酵母（Saccharomyces cerevisiae）稳健的乙醇发酵及代谢工程至关重要。然而，在遗传扰动下，防止糖酵解“涡轮式设计”结构过度激活的调控机制仍不清楚。本研究构建了包含90个反应和543个参数的酵母中心碳代谢动力学模型。研究者利用遗传算法，使用野生型菌株和11个单基因缺失突变株的多组学数据集（蛋白质组学、代谢组学及通量组学）训练模型集合。对校准模型开展代谢控制分析（MCA）发现，在本研究采用的培养条件下，所考察的大多数菌株主要由两种调控模式控制糖酵解通量；不过，gcr2Δ 表现出不同的控制特征，而模型无法重现 gnd1Δ 的行为。野生型、gcn4Δ 和 rpe1Δ 菌株表现为己糖激酶（HXK）受限的控制模式：降低的己糖激酶活性可能发挥反馈限流作用，以防止途径过度激活。相反，另外7个突变株转向 ATP 需求耦合模式，将通量控制转移到耗能反应，使糖酵解通量直接与 ATP 需求相联系。两组内部均未发现一致共享的单一调控基序，这意味着不同菌株各自的表达调整反复形成了这两种调控模式。这些发现阐明了酵母为维持高发酵能力而采用的稳健、多模式控制策略，并为靶向代谢工程和稳健生物工艺设计提供了理论基础。

papers.title: Molecular Biology and Synthetic Biology-Guided Development of Recognition and Reporting Elements of Biosensor.
papers.abstract: Microbial cell biosensors are capable of detecting fluctuations in the concentrations of substances both inside and outside the cell, as well as changes in the external environment, and can generate measurable signal outputs. Microbial cell biosensors are characterized by low cost, simple operation, and high specificity. The rapid advancement of synthetic biology has significantly propelled the development and practical application of microbial cell biosensors. In this chapter, we provide a comprehensive summary of the composition and working principles of microbial cell biosensors. Additionally, we introduce various strategies and the latest progress in modifying biorecognition element and reporting elements using molecular biology and synthetic biology techniques in recent years. This book chapter offers new insights and valuable references for the research and development of microbial cell biosensors.
papers.authors: Luo Y, Meng C, Wang L, Liang B.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (https://synbiofoodb.biodesign.ac.cn/), a knowledgebase dedicated to synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing. SynBioFooDB integrates 74 237 food-related compounds with standardized chemical identities and annotations covering food occurrence, bioactivity, toxicity, and regulatory information. It further provides expert-curated biomanufacturing evidence for 1054 compounds from 5592 publications, linking microbial hosts, substrates, genetic modifications, and quantitative production metrics through structured and traceable records. The database also contains 2002 literature-reported biosynthetic pathways for 971 compounds, enabling comparison of alternative precursors, enzyme combinations, and pathway architectures. For compounds without literature-reported pathways, SynBioFooDB provides computationally predicted candidate pathways to facilitate pathway prioritization and experimental evaluation. By integrating compound-level context, biomanufacturing evidence, and biosynthetic pathway information, SynBioFooDB supports systematic exploration, comparison, and rational design of microbial production strategies for food-related compounds.
papers.authors: Wei F, Deng X, Li H, Wang R, Mao Z, Mao Y, Liu Y, Niu Q, Qin Y, Du J, Liao X, Bai Y, Yuan Q, Ma H.

papers.title: "Illuminating" the silkworm chassis: Synthetic biology-driven evolution of genetic-based sexing circuits.
papers.abstract: The silkworm (Bombyx mori), a classical lepidopteran model, is evolving into a highly tractable synthetic biology chassis. In modern sericulture, genetic sexing circuits provide a rational design framework for efficient all-male rearing, effectively overcoming the gene dosage disruptions and fitness costs associated with traditional radiation-induced chromosomal translocations. This review systematically summarizes the construction strategies and industrial applications of these circuits. We outline the optimization of sex determination elements and highlight the advantages of far-red optical markers in penetrating host physical barriers and reducing cytotoxicity. Furthermore, we trace the evolution of genomic manipulation tools from random transposon insertions to targeted CRISPR/Cas9 integration into genomic safe harbors (GSHs). To address circuit instability during multigenerational rearing, protective molecular strategies-including boundary insulators, conditional expression, and automatic excision networks-are evaluated. We also explore the industrial interface that integrates standardized biological optical reporters with artificial intelligence and high-throughput optoelectronic sorting hardware. Ultimately, engineering principles derived from the silkworm chassis can provide a molecular framework for the sterile insect technique in global pest management, with future directions pointing toward footprint-free genome editing and dynamic conditional regulation.
papers.authors: Li C, Cao M, Li B.

papers.title: Multilevel metabolic engineering of Bacillus amyloliquefaciens for enhanced L-tyrosine production.
papers.abstract: L-Tyrosine is a valuable aromatic amino acid with diverse applications. Although plasmid-based overexpression has markedly improved L-tyrosine production, the dependence on antibiotic selection and genetic instability under nonselective conditions limits its industrial applicability. To address these issues, this study employed a multi-level metabolic engineering strategy to enhance the L-tyrosine biosynthetic pathway at the genomic level in Bacillus amyloliquefaciens. First, an expression cassette containing the mutant prephenate dehydrogenase (TyrAI309A/E330V) was inserted into the genome of the wild-type strain Z1. When the copy number reached three (strain Z4), L-tyrosine production reached 437.43mg/L. Subsequently, the mutant DAHP synthase (AroAR27A/K38A) was integrated, and the resulting two-copy strain Z7 increased L-tyrosine production to 591.29mg/L. Systematic identification of rate-limiting steps showed that most pathway genes enhanced production to varying extents. A promoter in situ replacement strategy was then applied to construct strain Z21, which further increased the titer to 813.01mg/L. Finally, by optimizing precursor supply, the engineered strain Z32 reached an L-tyrosine titer of 1079.94mg/L. Overall, this plasmid-free and antibiotic-independent platform offers a promising strategy for stable biosynthesis of L-tyrosine and other aromatic amino acids in microbial cell factories.
papers.authors: Zhang D, Jiang P, Wang L, Gu J, Ji A, Feng N.

papers.title: A cryptic lactate cycle in CO fermentation by Clostridium ljungdahlii .
papers.abstract: The valorization of C1 gases presents a route toward the utilization of industrial waste gases as resources. Acetogens such as Clostridium ljungdahlii serve as promising microbial cell factories for light-independent carbon fixation and high-value compound production, yet their efficiency is often limited by energy constraints and poorly understood metabolic pathways. Here, we investigated lactate metabolism in C. ljungdahlii during carbon monoxide (CO) fermentation via growth and product profiling, 13 C-labeling, gene knockouts, and transcriptomics. Although lactate cannot serve as the sole source of carbon and energy for C. ljungdahlii 's growth, we found that lactate can be co-fermented with CO into acetate. 13 C-tracing further revealed concurrent lactate production and oxidation during CO fermentation, with the unlabeled lactate fraction increasing from 1.0% (day 2) to 5.0% (day 6), indicating the existence of an active lactate cycle. Genetic and transcriptional analyses showed that lactate production and oxidation were catalyzed by two distinct lactate dehydrogenases: LdhA (CLJU_RS15865) and the electron-bifurcating Ldh/EtfAB_1 complex (CLJU_RS10590-CLJU_RS10600), respectively. Disruption of the lactate cycle, particularly in the Ldh/EtfAB_1 mutant, improved energy metabolism and triggered intracellular metabolic rearrangements. This mutant produced approximately 10-fold more lactate and shifted the acetate/ethanol ratio from 3.7:1 to 2.1:1, accompanied by upregulation of the AOR (aldehyde:ferredoxin oxidoreductase)-mediated ethanol production pathway. Subsequent ldhA overexpression further elevated lactate titer to ~2.5 mM, confirming the potential for lactate production from CO. The results imply that the cryptic lactate cycle dissipates energy but aids in intracellular redox balancing during CO fermentation. These findings provide new insights into the metabolic engineering of acetogens to produce target compounds, such as lactate and ethanol. Importance Acetogens possess a natural carbon fixation pathway, the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway, enabling them to fix CO or CO2 to produce acetate. Among various acetogens, Clostridium ljungdahlii exhibits strong tolerance to CO and thus holds great application potential for the resource utilization of syngas. However, the physiological and metabolic mechanisms underlying its autotrophic fermentation remain incompletely understood, which imposes limitations on metabolic engineering efforts. In this study, we systematically investigated lactate metabolism in C. ljungdahlii and revealed the existence of a cryptic lactate cycle during CO fermentation. By characterizing this cycle's operation and its impacts on energy metabolism and carbon distribution, we elucidated its potential physiological functions. These findings not only expand our understanding of the physiological and metabolic behaviors of acetogens during autotrophic fermentation but also provide theoretical guidance for the future metabolic engineering of lactate, ethanol, and other compounds.
papers.authors: Sun H, Yi J, Huang H, Wang S.

papers.title: Kinetic metabolic modeling of Saccharomyces cerevisiae mutants reveals two major regulatory patterns of glycolytic flux control.
papers.abstract: Maintaining a high glycolytic flux is critical for robust ethanol fermentation and metabolic engineering in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. However, the regulatory mechanisms that prevent the excess turbo design structure of glycolysis under genetic perturbations are unknown. In this study, we constructed a kinetic model of yeast central carbon metabolism encompassing 90 reactions and 543 parameters. Using a genetic algorithm, we trained the model ensemble using multi-omics datasets (proteomics, metabolomics, and fluxomics) collected from the wild-type strain and 11 single-gene deletion mutants. Metabolic control analysis (MCA) of the calibrated models revealed that two major regulatory modes governed the glycolytic flux in most of the strains examined under the culture condition used in this study, although gcr2Δ exhibited a distinct control profile and gnd1Δ could not be reproduced by the model. The wild-type, gcn4Δ, and rpe1Δ strains exhibited an HXK-limited control mode, in which lowered hexokinase activity likely acts as a feedback limiter to prevent pathway over-activation. Conversely, seven other mutants shifted to an ATP demand-coupled mode, transferring flux control to energy-dissipating reactions and linking glycolytic flux directly to ATP demand. No single motif was uniformly shared within either group, implying that strain-specific expression adjustments repeatedly resulted in two regulatory modes. These findings elucidate the robust, multimodal control strategies employed by yeast to safeguard its high fermentation capacity and provide a theoretical foundation for targeted metabolic engineering and robust bioprocess design.
papers.authors: Sato G, Yamasaki K, Okahashi N, Matsuda F.

papers.title: Enhanced violacein production by synthetically engineered mutualistic Escherichia coli co-culture biofilms in a spatially partitioned bioreactor system.
papers.abstract: Violacein (VIO) is a bacterial secondary metabolite with potential applications in healthcare, textile, and cosmetic industries. Although modular synthetic E. coli co-cultures are promising for biomanufacturing, VIO production in such systems depends on efficient cross-feeding, which requires spatial proximity and stable interactions among co-culture members. Here, we demonstrate that a spatially partitioned bioreactor can support coexisting suspended and carrier-associated states of a mutualistic recombinant E. coli co-culture, enabling direct comparison of their crude VIO production performance. The co-culture was cultivated in a spatially partitioned bioreactor consisting of an aerobic stirred-tank compartment connected to an oxygen-limited cartridge containing Fibra-Cel® discs as carriers, thereby enabling biomass partitioning into suspended and adherent fractions. Across three biological replicates, the adherent biofilm-associated fraction consistently exhibited higher biomass-normalized crude VIO production than the corresponding suspended fraction, with 4.51-, 20.05-, and 5.51-fold increases. Although the adherent fraction represented only 10.6-24.0% of the total biomass, it contributed 35.4-86.3% of the total crude VIO. These results show that carrier-associated spatial organization within the partitioned bioreactor supported the formation of highly productive biofilm-associated E. coli co-culture populations. The presented concept highlights the potential of spatially organized, carrier-associated co-cultures for the intensification of secondary metabolite production and future biofilm-based bioprocessing applications.
papers.authors: Gupta S, Takors R.

papers.title: Dynamic tapered nozzle and multiple waveform modulation enable high-speed piezoelectric jetting without satellite droplets across broad fluid property ranges.
papers.abstract: Piezoelectric drop-on-demand inkjet printing enables controlled microdroplet deposition in microfluidics, biomanufacturing, and precision manufacturing. However, conventional pressure chamber piezoelectric printheads are susceptible to viscous dissipation and nozzle clogging, exhibit limited adaptability to high-viscosity, low-surface-tension liquids and particle/cell suspensions, and struggle to suppress satellite droplets effectively. These limitations hinder their practical deployment in high-precision and high-stability inkjet applications. Here, a dynamic tapered nozzle generates droplets through local self-pumping induced by geometric deformation rather than pressure-wave propagation in a conventional pressure chamber. Structural optimization enabled droplet velocities of 5.42-12.67 m s -1 and stable ejection at viscosities up to 40.3 mPa s, surface tensions of 24.44-72.75 mN m -1 , and Z values of 1.01-38.11. Mechanistic analysis identified high-frequency residual nozzle oscillations as the primary cause of ligament stretching and secondary breakup. Based on this mechanism, a multiple waveform modulation strategy is devised to dynamically regulate the nozzle displacement response. This strategy effectively suppresses satellite droplets during high-speed ejection while maintaining printing throughput and achieves a 32% reduction in droplet diameter. The satellite-droplet suppression effect is further validated in a 0.5 wt% SiO 2 nanoparticle suspension and a 10 wt% PVP K30 solution. The platform enables high-viability printing of MC3T3 cells and carrier-free intracellular delivery of 70 kDa fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-dextran, establishing a feasible pathway for high-speed and stable ejection across broad fluid property ranges with low clogging risk.
